- **Server (migration):** `chat_channels.linked_type / linked_id / linked_at` (CHECKs: both or neither, `CHAT_LINK_TARGETS`, channels only; index). `conversation-of` joins `RELATION_KINDS` and `entity_links`' CHECK. `chat_op_link_channel(channel, type, id)` links, relinks or unlinks; `chat_op_create_channel` gains `p_link_type / p_link_id` (6-argument one dropped, re-granted); `chat_op_start_conversation(ws, type, id)` ("Start a conversation for X", CH56); `chat_conversations_for_item` gains the link half (relation `conversation-of`, read from the column) with `unread` and `archived`; `chat_link_files_here(channel)` for capture's destination. A trigger keeps `conversation-of` rows in step with the column. Activity `chat.channel_link`.
- **Contracts:** `CHAT_LINK_TARGETS` (+ parse/normalize/is), `RELATION_KINDS` + `conversation-of`, `USER_RELATION_KINDS` (the drop-link toast's kind menu uses it); drift gate for both CHECKs.
- **Chat:** Details' "Linked to" (`panel/link-section.tsx`): RF-1's live card (tombstone when archived or deleted), a team as its name and count, "Link to…" / Change / Unlink for posters in the conversation, the once-only "Add the team's 4 people?" offer. The toolbar's chip (`LinkChip`). New conversation's "Link to (optional)" between Name and People (frame 3); picking an item names an unnamed channel after it. Make a task files into the linked project when `chat_link_files_here` says so, else the Inbox. History line "linked this channel to a project / client / team", "unlinked this channel".
- **Items:** "Conversation: Acme · 3 new" (`ConversationLines`) in the project overview's `chat.conversation` slot (Tasks' `ProjectChatSlots`), and above "Mentioned in" in every item's Linked through `MentionedInLines` (so the client hubs get it via `LinkedSections`); a linked conversation's "Mentioned in" line is dropped. `conversation-of` rows stay out of link cards (rollup).
- **Start a conversation:** in the project's ⋯ (`plan-view-header.tsx`, edit access, not archived) and the company / contact hub's ⋯ (`canEdit`); it opens the new channel and refreshes the item's lines.

## Agent's choices (deferred to by Maciej: confirmed for building, may be reconsidered)

- **Linking needs being in the conversation, able to post in it, and edit rights on the item** (the orchestrator's rule over the brief's "see") · agent · a link writes onto the item's page · rejected: any reader.
- **Unlinking needs only being a poster in the conversation** · agent · it removes the conversation's own setting; requiring edit on an item that may be gone would strand a tombstone link · rejected: edit on the old item.
- **A team's "edit rights" = being in the team, its creator, the workspace owner or an admin** · agent · teams have no per-item grants; mirrors who may delete a team plus its people · rejected: anyone in the workspace.
- **An archived project can't be linked** · agent · its chip would be a tombstone from the start.
- **"Start a conversation" is its own op** (`chat_op_start_conversation`), calling `chat_op_create_channel` with the link · agent · the dialog's explicit name / privacy / people and the ⋯'s derived ones are different contracts · rejected: a "no name means derive" mode inside create.
- **"Start a conversation" isn't offered for a team** · agent · the spec places it on a project's ⋯ and a client's hub only.
- **The " 2" clash counts channels the creator can see, plus every public one** · agent · same as a rename; a private name nobody can see never leaks · rejected: all channels.
- **The column is the truth; the `conversation-of` row mirrors it** · agent · a team has no registry row, and item deletes soft-delete links; the item's "Conversation:" line, the chip and capture read the column, and a trigger refuses any `conversation-of` row (or kind change) that doesn't match it, and keeps a restored one deleted when the link has moved on · rejected: a session flag.
- **The link ops keep their own kind lists** (no `conversation-of`): only chat writes it. The MCP tools' `relation_kind` enum still lists `RELATION_KINDS` (brief), so it advertises a kind the op refuses (CV-21 may switch to `USER_RELATION_KINDS`).
- **"Conversation: Acme · 3 new" shows "· archived" for an archived channel, and no count at 0** · agent.
- **The line also shows in every item's Linked above "Mentioned in"** (the hub's row, AC6.1), and a linked conversation's own "Mentioned in" line is dropped · agent · one line per conversation.
- **Capture's destination comes from the server** (`chat_link_files_here`: a live, unarchived project the reader may edit) · agent · the client has no edit level per project.
- **Details' team row shows the team's name and its people count; the toolbar shows the team's name with a people glyph** · agent · RF-1 has no team kind.
- **The team offer appears right after linking a team, only for someone who may add people** (any poster on a public channel, managers on a private one), with Add / Not now · agent · "offers once".
- **New conversation's link field: a "A project, client or team" button opening the same picker, then the item's name, Change and Remove** · agent · frame 3 draws a filled field; the picker is the one Details uses.
- **A public conversation may link to an item only some people can see** · agent · the brief binds only "the caller can edit the item"; refusing would block the common agency case (a client record only its owner sees, the client's channel open to the team). People who can't open the item see RF-1's "Private item" on the chip and card, get no "Conversation:" line on it, and capture never files into it for them · rejected: refuse the link and ask for a private conversation.
- **An archived project reads "Website · archived"** in RF-1's tombstone look (the chip and card don't open it) · agent · whoever could open it keeps its name; a deleted one stays "Deleted project" with no title · rejected: "Archived project" with no name. **App-wide:** it is RF-1's shared resolver, so every project reference (notes, comments, task text, chat messages), not only Chat's chip, reads this way; it matches Tasks hiding archived projects. Needs a spine decision entry when this lands (Maciej's call to keep it app-wide).
- **Relinking to an item the conversation linked to before brings its old row back** (one row per conversation and item); linking again to the same item while its row is gone restores it, with no new history line and the link's date kept · agent.
- **A conversation's link row is changed only from the conversation:** the link ops' delete and Contacts' unlink refuse it (the item's own delete still closes it), and the client treats it as Chat's (`isChatOwnedLink`) · agent.
- **"Remove" in New conversation takes back the name the link filled in** (never a name you typed); picking another item renames an auto-filled name · agent.
- **Frame 7's "new linked channel" start block isn't built** · agent · the conversation-start block is CV-7a's; left for a polish pass.

## Gotchas (area: supabase / ui)

- `workspace_members.perms` is resolved from the role by a trigger: to make an admin in a SQL test, insert `role = 'admin'`, not `perms`.
- `src/features/chat/markup-v2/refs-parity.test.ts` skips without psql or the stack; set `MODUO_REQUIRE_DB=1` on a run that must check the server, and it fails instead. Opt-in only: nothing sets it yet (verify and CI still skip with a warning; `chat_links.test.sql` pins the grammar's edges on the server).

- Direct `INSERT INTO buckets` in a SQL test doesn't register the project in `entities`; the link op registers its target itself (the mirror needs the FK).
- The worktree guard refuses multi-line `cat >>` / `python -` heredocs touching repo files: edit through the editor tool.
